description: For each rating, divide the average rental rate by the average rental duration.

b.request: For each film rating, compute the rating's average rental_rate divided by its average rental_duration (average per-day rate), then among ratings whose per-day rate exceeds the simple mean of the five ratings' per-day rates, return one row with the average of their average film lengths (ignoring NULL lengths), the average of their per-day rates, and the average of their per-day rate minus that mean, all unrounded
b.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate) / AVG(rental_duration) AS pdr, AVG(length) AS avg_len FROM film GROUP BY rating), m AS (SELECT AVG(pdr) AS mean_pdr FROM r) SELECT AVG(r.avg_len) AS avg_length, AVG(r.pdr) AS avg_per_day_rate, AVG(r.pdr - m.mean_pdr) AS avg_diff FROM r CROSS JOIN m WHERE r.pdr > m.mean_pdr

c.request: For each film rating, look at its average film length (ignoring films with no length) and its rental rate per day of rental. Which ratings have a per-day rate above the simple mean of the ratings' per-day rates, with each rating counting once? For just those ratings, give one row with their average length, their average per-day rate, and the average amount by which they exceed that mean. Don't round anything. For each rating, divide the average rental rate by the average rental duration.
c.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(rental_rate) / AVG(rental_duration) AS per_day FROM film GROUP BY rating), m AS (SELECT AVG(per_day) AS mean_per_day FROM r) SELECT AVG(r.avg_length) AS avg_length, AVG(r.per_day) AS avg_per_day_rate, AVG(r.per_day - m.mean_per_day) AS avg_excess FROM r CROSS JOIN m WHERE r.per_day > m.mean_per_day

a.request: For each film rating, find the average film `length` (ignoring films with no length) and the per-day rental price, defined as the rating's average `rental_rate` divided by its average `rental_duration`. Then take the simple mean of those per-day prices across the ratings, with each rating counting once, and keep only the ratings whose per-day price is above that mean. For those ratings, give one row with the average of their average lengths, the average of their per-day prices, and the average amount by which their per-day price exceeds the cross-rating mean. Don't round anything.
a.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(rental_rate) / AVG(rental_duration) AS per_day FROM film GROUP BY rating), m AS (SELECT AVG(per_day) AS mean_per_day FROM r) SELECT AVG(r.avg_length) AS avg_of_avg_lengths, AVG(r.per_day) AS avg_per_day_price, AVG(r.per_day - m.mean_per_day) AS avg_excess FROM r CROSS JOIN m WHERE r.per_day > m.mean_per_day

d.request: For each film rating, calculate its average film length (ignoring films with no length) and its per-day rental rate, defined as the average rental rate divided by the average rental duration. Then find the ratings whose per-day rate is above the simple mean of all ratings' per-day rates, counting each rating once. For only those ratings, return a single row with their average film length, their average per-day rate, and the average amount by which their per-day rates exceed that mean. Don't round any values.
d.sql: WITH per_rating AS (SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(rental_rate) / AVG(rental_duration) AS per_day_rate FROM film GROUP BY rating), m AS (SELECT AVG(per_day_rate) AS mean_rate FROM per_rating) SELECT AVG(p.avg_length) AS avg_film_length, AVG(p.per_day_rate) AS avg_per_day_rate, AVG(p.per_day_rate - m.mean_rate) AS avg_excess FROM per_rating p CROSS JOIN m WHERE p.per_day_rate > m.mean_rate
